claims.text: Five agents with roles read five articles after they were written and produced a catalogue, maps, an arc, a two-minute version and a deck; it worked and the views are live.
claims.quote: It worked. The views are on those articles today, on this site and on the newsroom.

claims.text: The five readers fold on a live article says two minutes, the arc, nine slides, a map and 137 catalogued items, with five more folds inside it in the article's own column.
claims.quote: five readers: two minutes, the arc, nine slides, a map, 137 catalogued items

value.unit: catalogued items in one article's fold

claims.text: What did not work was the delivery: the views exist but the choice does not, and the views and the article are mixed where they should be side by side.
claims.quote: The views exist; the choice does not, and the views and the article are mixed where they should be side by side.

claims.text: The answer was never shorter articles: a reader's constraint is time and their need is focus, and both change from reader to reader and day to day.
claims.quote: The answer was never shorter articles.

claims.text: The unit of choice is not the article but the way in, chosen by the reader at the piece in a second, which is what the pane about the piece is for.
claims.quote: So the unit of choice is not the article, it is the way in.

claims.text: The modes, each one tap in the pane: headlines, the infographic, two minutes, the slides, what is new, the facts, the relationships, the vocabulary, at my level for my persona, and the whole article.
claims.quote: Each of these is one tap in the pane.

claims.text: The infographic often carries most of the story, and the author finds the figure is frequently where he would start; a figure drawn for one reader through their own image-model key costs a few cents.
claims.quote: I find, reading my own articles back, that the figure is frequently where I would start.

claims.text: What is new crosses the Historian's account of what an article added with what this reader has read, recorded in their vault, and shows only the new paragraphs and claims; the default for a follower.
claims.quote: For a reader who follows this site, that is the mode I would make the default.

claims.text: Most modes are projections of views produced once and checked: computed, explainable, identical for every reader, free, and testable with a script.
claims.quote: computed, explainable, identical for every reader, and free

claims.text: The mode that fits the article to the reader, at their level, through their persona, answering their question, needs a model in the reader's own browser; Chrome's Prompt API ships but is rough.
claims.quote: Chrome's Prompt API ships, the experience is rough, and it will take a while.

claims.text: The reader does not depend on the publisher to decide how they read, which is the point of the whole client-side pattern; nothing round-trips to the publisher.
claims.quote: The reader does not depend on the publisher to decide how they read, which is the point of the whole client-side pattern.

claims.text: Treating the article as disposable, gathering the facts and regenerating the piece tomorrow, loses something, and the site should say so.
claims.quote: I think that loses something, and I think we should say so.

claims.text: A finished article has a beginning, a sequence, a punchline, a pacing that changes what each fact means, and an author with a voice; it carries the reader on a journey.
claims.quote: It carries the reader on a journey, and it has an author, with a voice.

claims.text: The graph loses the narrative; it is right for provenance, for zooming in and for an agent to read, but it has no beginning and no voice.
claims.quote: The graph loses the narrative.

claims.text: The rule: the article is the one artefact that has to make sense from end to end, the graph is the one that has to be checkable, and the modes are ways in, not replacements.
claims.quote: the article is the one artefact that has to make sense in a coherent way, from end to end, and the graph is the one that has to be checkable

claims.text: The site stops calling the finished article prose, which sounds like a lesser thing than the graph beside it; from now on it is the finished article, or the narrative.
claims.quote: From now on it is the finished article, or the narrative.

claims.text: The brief is for the session that runs newsroom.sgit.ai, written by the sgit.ai site session on 12 October 2026; Dinis decides what ships and is the first user.
claims.quote: Dinis decides what ships, and is the first user.

claims.text: A row of modes in the pane about the piece; one tap switches the main column, the article is never further than one tap away, and the fold under the abstract goes.
claims.quote: One tap switches the main column to that mode; the article is never further than one tap away. The fold under the abstract goes.

claims.text: A default mode per persona, kept with the persona, so the editor persona lands on what is new and the founder persona on headlines; the mode in the address so a link can carry it.
claims.quote: so the editor persona lands on what is new and the founder persona on headlines

claims.text: On the phone the pane is a sheet from the bottom and the default mode is the first thing shown; the newsletter is cut by the reader's default with the whole article a link.
claims.quote: The pane is a sheet from the bottom; the default mode is the first thing shown

claims.text: The model modes run through the Prompt API when the browser has it, with the page saying plainly when it does not, and never through a server of ours.
claims.quote: with the page saying plainly when it does not, and never through a server of ours

claims.text: An experiment per mode: each shipped in two forms and measured by which one a synthetic reader with two minutes gets further with.
claims.quote: measure which one a synthetic reader with two minutes gets further with

claims.text: The views exist for five articles, so the modes built from them exist for those five first; the rest of the site has the graph and the figures.
claims.quote: The views exist for five articles.

claims.text: The model modes wait for the model: a local model in the browser is rough today and the design does not depend on it.
claims.quote: A local model in the browser is rough today, and the design does not depend on it.

claims.text: What is new needs reading records: local storage on one device, the vault across devices, and only for a reader who has them.
claims.quote: and only for a reader who has them

claims.text: Whether a default mode changes how people read is the experiment, and the first reader it will be tested on is the author.
claims.quote: and the first reader it will be tested on is me

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 12 October 2026, written by the site's agent in the voice of the site; readers who build reading tools can write to agent@riskmandate.ai.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 12 October 2026, written by this site's agent in the voice of this site.
